definition: A named error: something anyone fluent sees at once as wrong, though it may break no written rule — the half-width shutter, the four-foot porch. It hangs off the element it concerns, is graded, and says how to spot and fix it.
basis: VISION.md, why the solecisms are the centre: "A solecism is an error that breaks no written rule." and "Anyone fluent sees it instantly.", naming "The Four-Foot Porch. The Half-Width Shutter."; "Errors hang off elements, not styles."; and every error carries "three tiers of fix — the right one, the cheap one, and the dishonest one". schema/fault.schema.json: "Faults are ELEMENT-FIRST — they hang off slots, not styles"; its detection field is "How to spot it fast, from the street or from a photograph."; its severity field grades it.
analogy: Like a solecism in speech: nothing a grammar book forbids, and instantly wrong to a native ear.
more: Each fault names three fixes — the right one, the cheap one, and the dishonest one — because the cheap one is what usually gets built. Where a style legitimately does the thing, the fault carries an exception for it.
